display.title: Tanya Shiur 35: Chapter 24 and a Child's Brachah on Water (After Shavuos)
display.summary_short: A Yiddish shiur: the Rebbe's Shavuos talk on children as the guarantors of the Torah, Tanya chapter 24 on the nations and Hashem's will, and a Baal Shem Tov story about redeeming captives.
display.summary_long: Shiur 35 in Rabbi Yosef Goldstein's Yiddish Tanya series opens with a point from the Rebbe's Shavuos talk: Hashem accepted the Jewish children as guarantors for the Torah, and teaching a small child to make a brachah on a glass of water teaches him that Hashem watches every detail and that one may not take what is not his. The sun shining through millions of windows at once shows how Hashem hears every child's brachah, and a melamed explains to his pupil why he pauses before each brachah to think to Whom he is speaking. The class then studies Tanya chapter 24: the nations believe in a G-d too lofty to watch the earth, yet they cannot act against His will, and their life comes to them only 'from behind'. Redeeming the G-dly sparks in food by eating for Hashem's sake is a daily pidyon shvuyim, illustrated by a Baal Shem Tov story: a poor young couple spend their wedding money to free a family jailed by a poritz, and the playful wedding gifts of the Baal Shem Tov's students later come true. The class ends with how even a small sin separates a Jew from Hashem, and why this lowest world is the purpose of creation.
display.lesson: Hashem watches over every detail, even a child's brachah; and freeing another Jew, in body or in spirit, brings great blessing.

segments.title: The Rebbe's Shavuos talk: children as guarantors
segments.summary: Hashem gave the Torah in the merit of the children, and a child's brachah on water teaches emunah and honesty.

segments.title: The sun through a million windows
segments.summary: As the sun shines into every window at once, Hashem hears every child's brachah.

segments.title: Why the melamed paused before each brachah
segments.summary: A pupil asks his teacher why he touches his forehead before every brachah, and learns to think to Whom he is speaking.

segments.title: Tanya chapter 24: the nations and Hashem's will
segments.summary: The nations believe in a G-d above other powers but cannot act against His will; their life comes 'from behind' and the G-dly spark in them is in exile.

segments.title: Eating for Hashem's sake: a daily pidyon shvuyim
segments.summary: A moment's thought before eating redeems the G-dly spark in the food.

segments.title: The Baal Shem Tov and the wedding gifts
segments.summary: A poor young couple use their wedding money to free a captive family, and the joking gifts of the Baal Shem Tov's students later come true.

segments.title: Daniel in the lions' den and the Name on the forehead
segments.summary: A tzaddik's holiness protects him, as the Name Shakai on the mezuzah guards a Jewish home.
